about: The scripted AI lesson for g5-development (2026-11-19, Phase B, brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md): every word she sees is written here once and checked (tools/check-script.js, tools/review-lesson.js --script). The AI only marks her typed answers (choosing a branch written here), answers her own questions, and sorts her messages. It opens with two maths questions (the mean, and an amount per person) that the lesson builds on.

keyPoints.heading: What is development and how do we measure it?

steps.text: Welcome! This lesson is about why some countries are much richer and healthier than others, how we measure the difference, and what people do to close it.

steps.question: First, two quick maths questions you will need. Four friends have £2, £4, £6 and £8. What is the mean amount?
steps.right: Yes: add them up (£20) and share by 4: £5 each.

wrong.other: Not quite: £5. Add them up to £20, then divide by 4.
wrong.total: Nearly: £20 is the total. The mean shares it out: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.
wrong.mid: Not quite: the mean is the total shared out equally: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.

idk.hint: Add the four amounts, then divide by how many friends there are.

steps.answerWhy: The mean is the total shared out equally: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.

steps.question: Second: a country earns £100 million in a year and has 10 million people. How much is that per person?
steps.right: Yes: £100 million ÷ 10 million = £10 per person.

wrong.other: Not quite: £10. Share the total by the number of people: £100 million ÷ 10 million.
wrong.times: Not quite: per person means share it out, so divide: £100 million ÷ 10 million = £10.
wrong.minus: Not quite: per person means share it out, so divide: £100 million ÷ 10 million = £10.

idk.hint: Per person means shared out equally. Divide the total by the number of people.

steps.answerWhy: £100 million shared between 10 million people is £10 each.

steps.text: Now this lesson. Development means people's quality of life getting better: richer, healthier and better educated. To compare countries, geographers use measures.

Measures about money are called economic measures. The main one is GNI per head (gross national income per head): all the income a country earns in a year, divided by its number of people. It is the mean income for each person.

steps.question: In 2025, GNI per head was about $54,550 in the UK and $1,360 in Nigeria. Roughly how many times more, per person, did the UK earn?
steps.right: Yes: 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40. That gap is what this lesson is about.

wrong.other: Not quite: about 40 times. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.
wrong.four: Not quite: 4 × 1,360 is only about 5,440. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.
wrong.four100: Not quite: 400 × 1,360 would be over half a million. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.

idk.hint: Divide 54,550 by 1,360. Is the answer nearer 4, 40 or 400?

steps.answerWhy: 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40, so the UK earned about 40 times more per person.

steps.text: Measures about people's lives are called social measures. Life expectancy is how long a baby born now can expect to live: about 84 years in Japan and 55 in Nigeria.
The infant mortality rate is the number of babies who die before their first birthday, for every 1,000 born alive, in a year. In Japan it is about 2; in Nigeria about 70.

steps.question: Country A loses 30 babies per 1,000 before age one; Country B loses 5. Which country is probably more developed?
steps.right: Yes: a lower infant mortality rate usually means better health care, food and clean water.

wrong.other: Not quite: Country B.
wrong.a: Not quite: more babies dying is a sign of poorer health care. Country B, with 5 per 1,000, is probably more developed.
wrong.cannot: One measure is not the whole picture, but it is a strong clue: Country B, with fewer babies dying, is probably more developed.

idk.hint: Fewer babies dying is a sign of good health care. Which country has fewer?

steps.answerWhy: Country B: fewer babies dying usually means better health care, so it is probably more developed.

steps.text: Other social measures are people per doctor, the share of adults who can read and write, and access to safe water.
The HDI, or Human Development Index, combines three things into one score between 0 and 1: income, life expectancy and education. Nearer 1 means more developed.
Every measure has a limitation: a reason it can give a misleading picture.

steps.question: GNI per head is a mean. In a country where a few people are very rich and most are poor, why can it mislead?

options.text: The rich few push the mean up, so most people earn far less

steps.right: Yes: a mean hides how unequally money is shared. That is a limitation.

wrong.other: Not quite: the rich few push the mean up, so most people earn far less than it.
wrong.twice: Not quite: people are counted once. The problem is that the rich few push the mean up, hiding how poor most people are.
wrong.farmers: Partly: food that farmers grow to eat is often missed, which is a real limitation. But the bigger problem here is that the rich few push the mean up, hiding how poor most people are.

idk.hint: The mean of £1, £1, £1 and £97 is £25. Does £25 describe what most people have?

steps.answerWhy: A mean can be pushed up by a rich few, so GNI per head hides how unequally money is shared.

steps.text: Other limitations: how many babies are born depends on religion and culture, not only on development, and figures from poorer countries can be out of date or guessed. One measure on its own never gives the whole picture.

steps.prompt: In one line: what does the HDI combine?
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the HDI combines income, life expectancy and education into one score.

steps.text: The World Bank, an international organisation that lends money for development, sorts countries into groups by GNI per head.
A rich country, such as the UK or Japan, is called an HIC: a high income country.
One of the poorest countries, such as Niger or Malawi, is called an LIC: a low income country.
In between are middle income countries, split into upper-middle and lower-middle income. Kenya is lower-middle income: still a poorer country.

A country whose economy has started to grow fast as it builds up industry is called an NEE: a newly emerging economy, such as China, India, Brazil or Nigeria. This label is not one of the World Bank groups.

steps.question: Most people in one country work on small farms, and it earns about $650 per person a year, half of Nigeria's figure: which group is it in?
steps.right: Yes: with such a low income per person, it is an LIC.

wrong.other: Not quite: an LIC, a low income country.
wrong.hic: Not quite: $650 a year is very low. It is an LIC.
wrong.nee: Not quite: nothing says its economy is growing fast through industry. With $650 a year it is an LIC.

idk.hint: The UK's GNI per head is $54,550 and Nigeria's $1,360. LICs have the lowest of all. Where does $650 fit?

steps.answerWhy: With about $650 per person a year, it is one of the poorest countries: an LIC.

steps.text: An older way of splitting the world is the Brandt Line, drawn on a world map to divide a richer "North" from a poorer "South". The line bends south to put rich Australia and New Zealand in the "North". It is out of date: fast-growing countries such as China lie in its "South".

steps.prompt: In one line: what is an NEE?
points: a country whose economy is growing fast as it builds up industry
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: an NEE is a newly emerging economy, growing fast as it builds up industry.

keyPoints.heading: Population and development: the Demographic Transition Model

steps.text: As a country develops, its births and deaths change in a pattern. The birth rate is the number of babies born for every 1,000 people each year.
The death rate is the number of people who die for every 1,000 people each year.
The Demographic Transition Model, or DTM, shows how the two rates change over five stages as a country develops.
Stage 1: both rates are high. Births and deaths roughly cancel out, so the population stays about the same.
Stage 2: the death rate falls fast, as clean water, food and health care improve, but the birth rate stays high.

steps.question: Predict: in stage 2, what happens to the size of the population?
steps.right: Yes: far more people are born than die, so it grows fast.

wrong.other: Not quite: it grows fast, because far more are born than die.
wrong.shrink: Not quite: births are still high while deaths are falling, so far more people are born than die. It grows fast.
wrong.same: Not quite: births are now much higher than deaths, so the population grows fast.

idk.hint: Are more people being born, or dying?

steps.answerWhy: Births stay high while deaths fall, so far more people are born than die: the population grows fast.

steps.text: Many LICs are in stage 2 today.
Stage 3: the birth rate falls too, as fewer babies die and more girls stay at school. Population growth slows. Many NEEs are here.
Stage 4: both rates are low, so the population stays steady. Most HICs, such as the UK, are here.
Stage 5: births fall below deaths, so the population slowly shrinks, as in Japan.

steps.question: Why can moving into stage 3 help a country's economy?

options.text: With fewer children to look after, more women can go out to work
Families need more children to help on farms

steps.right: Yes: more people working means more money earned and more tax collected.

wrong.other: Not quite: with fewer children to look after, more women can work.
wrong.farm: Not quite: in stage 3 families have fewer children. With fewer to look after, more women can work.
wrong.fewer: Not quite: people still need jobs. With fewer children to look after, more women can go out to work.

idk.hint: In stage 3 families have fewer children. Who is then freer to go out to work?

steps.answerWhy: With fewer children to look after, more women can go out to work, which helps the economy.

steps.prompt: In one line: which DTM stage are many LICs in, and why does their population grow fast?
points: the death rate has fallen but the birth rate is still high
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: many LICs are in stage 2, where the death rate has fallen but the birth rate is still high.

steps.text: Development is uneven: some countries are far ahead of others. The difference between the richest and poorest countries is called the development gap.
The causes of the gap come in three groups: physical, economic and historical.
Physical causes come from nature. A landlocked country, with no coastline, pays more to send goods abroad.
Drought and poor soils ruin crops. Natural hazards, such as floods and earthquakes, wreck homes and roads. Diseases such as malaria stop people working.
Economic causes come from trade and money. Many poorer countries rely on selling raw materials, such as coffee or copper. Raw materials sold like this are called primary products.
Primary products earn little and their prices swing up and down, while goods made in factories cost a lot to buy. Paying back debts also leaves less money for schools and hospitals.

Historical causes come from the past. Colonialism is when one country rules another for its own benefit: European countries ruled much of Africa and Asia, took raw materials and drew borders that split peoples.

steps.question: Which of these is a physical cause of uneven development?

options.text: Floods that wreck farms and roads

steps.right: Yes: a flood is a natural hazard, so it is physical.

wrong.other: Not quite: floods. Physical means it comes from nature.
wrong.debt: Not quite: debt is about money, an economic cause. Physical means from nature, like a flood.
wrong.borders: Not quite: colonial borders come from history. Physical means from nature, like a flood.

idk.hint: Physical means it comes from nature. Which option is about water and weather?

steps.answerWhy: A flood comes from nature, so it is a physical cause.

steps.text: Uneven development has consequences. There are big differences, called disparities, in wealth and in health between countries.
Uneven development also causes international migration: people moving to live in another country.

steps.question: Why do many people migrate from poorer countries to richer ones?

options.text: Because richer countries have more farmland
Because poorer countries have better hospitals

steps.right: Yes: the gap in jobs and pay pulls people to richer countries, along with safety and better services.

wrong.other: Not quite: for jobs and higher pay.
wrong.farm: Not quite: most migrants do not move to farm. They move for jobs and higher pay.
wrong.hosp: Not quite: richer countries usually have better hospitals. People move for jobs and higher pay.

idk.hint: If wages in one country are many times higher, why might some people move there?

steps.answerWhy: People move from poorer to richer countries for jobs, higher pay and safety.

steps.text: Many migrants send part of their pay home to their families.

steps.prompt: In one line: name the three groups of causes of uneven development.
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the causes of uneven development are physical, economic and historical.

keyPoints.heading: Strategies to reduce the development gap

steps.text: Several strategies try to close the gap. Investment means companies or other countries putting money into businesses, roads and factories.
Industrial development means building up factories and industry. It brings jobs and wages, and the government can tax them.
Aid is help from one country or charity to another: money, goods or skills, given free or lent cheaply. Emergency aid helps after a disaster; long-term aid pays for schools or wells.
Aid can save lives, but it can be wasted, or a country can come to depend on it.
Debt relief cancels some of the money a poor country owes. Money that would have gone on repayments can then go on health and schools instead.

steps.question: A country's debts to other governments are cancelled. Which strategy is this?
steps.right: Yes: cancelling debt is debt relief. It is not a loan: it takes debt away.

wrong.other: Not quite: debt relief.
wrong.loan: Not quite: a loan adds debt. Cancelling debt is debt relief.
wrong.micro: Not quite: aid is help given or lent. Cancelling money a country already owes is debt relief.

idk.hint: Does this add to what the country owes, or take some away?

steps.answerWhy: Cancelling money a country owes is debt relief; it is not a loan.

steps.text: Microfinance means very small loans to people too poor to use an ordinary bank, to start a small business. Grameen Bank in Bangladesh lends mostly to women.
Intermediate technology is simple equipment local people can make, use and mend, such as a hand water pump.
Fairtrade pays farmers a fair minimum price for their crop, plus extra money for their community.

steps.question: A village gets a pump its own people can build and repair. Which strategy is this?
steps.right: Yes: simple kit the village can mend itself is intermediate technology.

wrong.other: Not quite: intermediate technology.
wrong.fair: Not quite: Fairtrade is about prices for farmers' crops. A pump the village can mend is intermediate technology.
wrong.micro: Not quite: microfinance is a small loan. A pump the village can mend is intermediate technology.

idk.hint: Which strategy is about simple equipment that local people can fix?

steps.answerWhy: A pump local people can build and repair is intermediate technology.

steps.text: Tourism brings money and jobs. In Kenya, international tourists grew from about 1.2 million in 2015 to about 2 million in 2019, for safaris and beaches.
In 2019 tourism earned Kenya $1.76 billion, about 15% of what Kenya earns from selling goods and services to other countries. That money pays wages, and taxes on it help pay for new roads.

steps.question: Which is a weakness of tourism as a way to close the gap?

options.text: Some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies
It gives jobs to local people

steps.right: Yes: money that goes abroad does not help Kenya. Visitor numbers also fall after terrorism or a pandemic.

wrong.other: Not quite: some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies.
wrong.jobs: Not quite: jobs are a strength. A weakness is that some money goes to foreign hotel companies.
wrong.earns: Not quite: that is a strength. A weakness is that some money goes to foreign hotel companies.

idk.hint: Many big hotels in Kenya belong to companies from richer countries. Where might their profit go?

steps.answerWhy: Some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies, and visitor numbers fall after terrorism or a pandemic.

steps.prompt: In one line: what is the difference between debt relief and microfinance?
points: debt relief cancels money a country owes
microfinance is a small loan to a person
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: debt relief cancels money a country owes, while microfinance is a small loan to a person.

steps.text: Is the development gap closing? The picture is mixed. Some NEEs, especially China and India, have grown fast, and hundreds of millions of their people now have higher incomes.
Extreme poverty means living on less than $3 a day. The share of the world's people in extreme poverty fell from about 43% in 1990 to about 10% in 2024.
But progress is uneven: many of the poorest countries, especially in Africa, are falling further behind.

steps.question: So, is the development gap closing? Which is the best overall judgement?

options.text: The gap is closing for some countries but widening for others

steps.right: Yes: that judgement uses evidence from both sides.

wrong.other: Not quite: closing for some, widening for others.
wrong.all: Not quite: many of the poorest countries are falling behind, so it has not closed everywhere.
wrong.none: Not quite: extreme poverty fell from about 43% to 10%, so a lot has changed for some countries.

idk.hint: There is evidence of progress and evidence of countries falling behind. Which option uses both?

steps.answerWhy: The gap is closing for fast-growing countries but widening for many of the poorest.

steps.text: To speed up progress, the United Nations, which almost every country belongs to, has set Sustainable Development Goals: targets to end poverty and hunger and improve health and schooling everywhere.

steps.prompt: In one line: is the development gap closing? Give one point each way.
points: it is closing for fast-growing countries
many of the poorest countries are falling behind
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the development gap is closing for fast-growing countries such as China, but many of the poorest African countries are falling behind.

steps.text: Now for a short quiz: six questions on the whole lesson. Take your time.

steps.question: Quiz, question 1 of 6: what does the HDI combine?
steps.right: Yes: income, life expectancy and education.

wrong.other: Not quite: income, life expectancy and education.
wrong.w1: Not quite: income alone is GNI per head. The HDI adds life expectancy and education.
wrong.w2: Not quite: the HDI combines income, life expectancy and education.

steps.answerWhy: The HDI combines income, life expectancy and education.

steps.question: Quiz, question 2 of 6: the birth rate is the number of babies born…?
steps.right: Yes: per 1,000 people each year.

wrong.other: Not quite: for every 1,000 people each year.
wrong.w1: Not quite: a rate is not a total. It is per 1,000 people each year.
wrong.w2: Not quite: the birth rate is per 1,000 people each year.

steps.answerWhy: The birth rate is births for every 1,000 people each year.

steps.question: Quiz, question 3 of 6: which DTM stage are most HICs, such as the UK, in?
steps.right: Yes: stage 4, with low birth and death rates.

wrong.other: Not quite: stage 4.
wrong.w1: Not quite: stage 2 has a high birth rate; many LICs are there. Most HICs are in stage 4.
wrong.w2: Not quite: stage 1 has high birth and death rates. Most HICs are in stage 4.

steps.answerWhy: Most HICs are in stage 4: low birth and death rates.

steps.question: Quiz, question 4 of 6: which is a historical cause of uneven development?
steps.right: Yes: colonialism comes from the past.

wrong.other: Not quite: colonialism.
wrong.w1: Not quite: drought is physical. Colonialism is historical.
wrong.w2: Not quite: that is economic. Colonialism is historical.

steps.answerWhy: Colonialism is a historical cause.

steps.question: Quiz, question 5 of 6: which strategy gives very small loans to start a business?
steps.right: Yes: microfinance.

wrong.other: Not quite: microfinance.
wrong.w1: Not quite: debt relief cancels money owed. Microfinance gives small loans.
wrong.w2: Not quite: Fairtrade pays farmers a fair price. Microfinance gives small loans.

steps.answerWhy: Microfinance gives very small loans to start a business.

steps.question: Quiz, question 6 of 6: why can GNI per head mislead?

options.text: It is a mean, which hides inequality

steps.right: Yes: a mean hides how unequally money is shared.

wrong.other: Not quite: it is a mean, which hides inequality.
wrong.w1: Not quite: it is measured for nearly every country. It misleads because it is a mean that hides inequality.
wrong.w2: Not quite: it is all about money. It misleads because it is a mean that hides inequality.

steps.answerWhy: GNI per head is a mean, so it hides inequality.

steps.text: That's the end of the quiz: you got {right} out of {n}.
